sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. U.P. Lko. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Bare Lal Bhartiya,Indra Pratap Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Jaikaran
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Jaikaran, learned counsel for the respondent no.2 as
well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.  In terms of the F.I.R., it was alleged that on 15.2.2024, the daughter of the informant was being misbehaved by the applicant which was seen by the informant herself.
The age of the victim was disclosed as 14 years.

In the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she knew the applicant for the last two months and on the date of incident, the applicant caught hold of her and was misbehaved which was seen by her mother.
However, in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. recorded after about one month, the victim stated that wrong was also committed on her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that there is contradiction in the statements of the victim recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
The medical on record does not corroborate the allegations of rape.
The tentative age of the victim is about 16- 18 years.
Hence, the applicant who is languishing in jail since 16.2.2024 having no criminal history, may be granted bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.

5. Considering the huge variance in the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. which are not corroborated by the medical on record, prima facie a case for bail is made out particularly when the applicant is in custody since 16.2.2024 having no criminal history, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Satendra Kumar be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.68 of 2024 under Sections 376(3), 504, 506 I.P.C., Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Mahrajganj, District Raebareli on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 12.7.2024 Shukla  Satendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138033661/
